newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Shell Brasil to invest $50 mln reais in gas firm.
newsitem.headline: Shell Brasil to invest $50 mln reais in gas firm.

text.p: Shell Brasil SA, a unit of Royal Dutch Shell, will invest 50 million reais ($48.1 million) in newly-acquired Brazilian gas company Petrogaz Distribuidora SA, the president of Shell Brasil said.

Shell Brasil bought privately-owned Petrogaz for an undisclosed sum in a bid to strengthen its position in Brazil's promising gas market. The price paid for Petrogaz could not be revealed due to a confidentiality clause in the contract.
Shell Brasil President Willem Goebel said Shell would invest 50 million reais ($48.1 million) in Petrogaz over the next five years to modernize the liquified petroleum gas (LPG) distributor.
Petrogaz has a four-percent share of Brazil's six-million-tonne-per-year LPG market and Shell hopes to increase the market share to well above 10 percent, Goebel said.
He said the potential for industrial use of LPG, which is currently used mainly for domestic purposes, was large in Brazil as was the possibility to use LPG for power generation purposes.

Corporate Affairs Director Gilbert Landsberg said Shell was looking into power generation as a new area for the company. He said Shell was running four projects around the world, including one in Brazil's northeastern state of Pernambuco, studying the feasibility of power generation with gas.
Shell, the largest natural gas company in the world, sells six million tonnes of LPG per year worldwide.
Goebel said Petrogaz was the company's first step into Brazil's LPG market, and Shell was the first fuel distributor in Brazil to move into LPG.
Petrogaz has an annual turnover of 80 million reais ($76.9 million) and LPG sales of 240,000 tonnes.

Goebel said the purchase price and investment in Petrogaz were in addition to Shell Brasil's planned investments for 1997 of $200 million in the oil and petrochemical sector and $100 million in the natural gas sector.

Petrogaz is Shell's second acquisition in the Brazilian gas sector in recent weeks. In January, the firm paid 74 million reais ($71.2 million) for a 20-percent stake in Sao Paulo state-owned Comgas, which is due to be privatized in October.
Goebel said Shell was not excluding the possibility of further acquisitions in the gas sector.
((Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
